transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because... my mind just won't hold onto things anymore. I'll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program, which is something I could do in my sleep before, and the numbers and the words just scatter on me. I just can't seem to focus my thoughts.
When did you first notice this change in your thinking?
It's been going on for about three weeks now. It started right around the time... well, ever since my older sister died.
Since your sister died, have you been feeling sad or down most of the day on most days?

Yes, I have. Most days I wake up with this... heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It just doesn't really go away. Even when my wife is sitting right there, talking kindly to me, I just feel like I'm sitting at the bottom of a well.
Since your sister died, have you lost interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy?

Yes, I have. I just... I haven't even touched the wood pieces sitting on my bench. I've skipped out on choir planning, and my chess games. Even fishing... well, it just sounds like more effort than it's worth right now. Which really is not like me at all.
Have you had any thoughts of killing yourself or that you would be better off dead?

Yes, I have. I just keep thinking that my family might be better off without me. And... well, honestly, when I'm near my workshop, I actually get a little scared of where my thoughts could go if I were left alone out there.
Have you made a specific plan for how you would kill yourself?

No, I haven't. I don't have a specific plan. Like I said, it's more just... a fear of what might happen if I'm out there in the shop with the tools. But I haven't actually sat down and figured out a way to do it or anything like that.
How has your sleep been since your sister died?
Honestly, I haven't really noticed a difference with my sleep. I guess... well, it's just been about the same as always. I still go to bed and wake up around my usual times.
Since your sister died, have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy during the day?
No, not really. I mean, I feel down, obviously, but physically... no, I haven't been feeling unusually tired or anything like that. My energy levels seem pretty normal for me.
Since your sister died, have you been feeling excessively guilty about yourself or about what happened?
No, I don't think so. I mean... I miss her terribly, of course, but I don't blame myself for what happened. It's just a terrible loss. But I haven't been feeling guilty about it, no.
Since your sister died, have you noticed any change in your appetite?

Yes, actually. Food has mostly lost its appeal lately. I usually just end up pushing my breakfast around the plate. By the time supper rolls around, my wife is having to remind me that I've barely eaten anything all day. I just don't have much interest in it right now.
